caption:
Use map when you want a new array built from the old one (rendering a list in React, converting prices).

Use forEach when you only want side effects and don't need a result (logging, pushing to analytics).

Common bug: using map, ignoring its result, and getting an ESLint warning. Or using forEach inside JSX and rendering nothing.

Neither one works with await the way you expect. For async loops, use for...of or Promise.all.

Source: MDN, Array.prototype.map() and forEach().
